story.title: Trump Jokes About 2028 Run at Rescheduled White House Correspondents' Dinner
story.summary: During the rescheduled White House Correspondents' Dinner, President Trump delivered a speech that included jokes about running for a third presidential term in 2028, despite constitutional restrictions. He also criticized the press and his political opponents, reflecting on his relationship with the media. The event took place after the original dinner was canceled due to a shooting incident in April.

explore_lenses.label: Could Trump legally seek a third term?
explore_lenses.title: The Constitution bars a third election
explore_lenses.summary: Trump’s remarks were presented as jokes, but the Twenty-Second Amendment states that no person may be elected president more than twice. Changing that limit would require a constitutional amendment, not merely a campaign announcement.

claims.text: The National Archives’ text of the Twenty-Second Amendment says that no person may be elected to the presidency more than twice.

Article V requires a proposed constitutional amendment to receive approval from two-thirds of both houses of Congress, or a convention called by two-thirds of state legislatures, and ratification by three-fourths of the states.

Rep. Daniel Goldman’s H.Res.171, which was referred to the House Judiciary Committee in February 2025, states the view that the Twenty-Second Amendment applies to two terms in the aggregate and prohibits Trump from another presidential run; it is a resolution, not a constitutional amendment or binding court ruling.

explore_lenses.label: What changed after the April shooting?
explore_lenses.title: A halted April gala became a smaller July event
explore_lenses.summary: The July 24 gathering was not simply the annual dinner moved on the calendar: it followed an April 25 attack that interrupted the original event. The correspondents’ association said it chose to hold a new dinner after member input, with enhanced security and access procedures.

claims.text: The Justice Department says the April 25 dinner at the Washington Hilton was interrupted when the defendant allegedly ran through a Secret Service screening checkpoint and shot an officer; President Trump was present at the event.
WHCA President Weijia Jiang said the board’s decision to schedule a July 24 replacement dinner followed member input and included significantly enhanced safety measures and new access procedures.
Reporting on the July event placed it at the Waldorf Astoria with about 700 guests, a smaller gathering than the disrupted April event.

explore_lenses.label: What happens next in the shooting case?
explore_lenses.title: The prosecution remains pretrial
explore_lenses.summary: The alleged gunman has been indicted and has pleaded not guilty; the case had not reached a trial date as of July 25. The next publicly reported status hearing is scheduled for August 20, when a trial schedule could be addressed.

claims.text: A federal grand jury returned a four-count indictment charging Cole Tomas Allen with attempted assassination of the president, assault on a federal officer with a deadly weapon, interstate transportation of a firearm and ammunition with intent to commit a felony, and discharging a firearm during a crime of violence.
Allen pleaded not guilty at his May 11 arraignment, according to Associated Press reporting.
At a June 29 status hearing, prosecutors said no plea offer had been made and that discovery was being provided to the defense; another hearing was set for August 20, when a trial date could be set.

related_stories.title: Trump Issues Order for Warnings on 'Inaccurate' History at Smithsonian
related_stories.summary: President Donald Trump has issued an executive order requiring the installation of signage at the Smithsonian's National Museum of American History. The signs will warn visitors about what the administration deems 'inaccurate historical information' within the museum. This move follows ongoing accusations from the Trump administration of anti-American bias in the museum's exhibits.

related_stories.title: Indian Education Minister Resigns Amid Youth Protests Over Exam Scandal
related_stories.summary: Dharmendra Pradhan has resigned as India's education minister following widespread protests by youth over exam paper leaks. The protests, led by a movement referred to as 'Cockroach,' culminated in celebrations among demonstrators after Pradhan's resignation was announced. The movement's leaders indicated that the government had accepted their demands, leading to the decision to end the protests.

related_stories.title: Democrats Select South Carolina for First Presidential Primary in 2028
related_stories.summary: The Democratic National Committee has recommended that South Carolina hold the first presidential primary for the 2028 election cycle. This decision marks a significant shift in the primary calendar, as South Carolina will replace Iowa as the opening contest. The move aims to prioritize representation among Black and Latino voters, with Nevada also scheduled for an early primary.

related_stories.title: International Criminal Court Votes to Remove Chief Prosecutor Karim Khan
related_stories.summary: The International Criminal Court (ICC) has voted to remove Chief Prosecutor Karim Khan amid allegations of sexual misconduct. The decision comes nearly two years after the allegations first emerged. Khan has denied the accusations, which include claims of engaging in an improper relationship with a junior staff member and attempting to prevent her from pursuing her complaint.
